title: Brodotrogir workers' reported January protest
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Employee counts250–280 or unpaid workers40/50 are not protest attendance.

start_date.summary: Month only provisionally from inaccessible February report's search discovery of a mid-January protest; day not established.

location.summary: Brodotrogir shipyard in Trogir; precise protest site rests on search-only retrospective lead.

organizer.summary: Worker involvement reported, but organizer of a January gathering unverified.

demands.summary: Unpaid wages and requests for government intervention appear in related reporting; linkage to public protest pending.

participants.summary: Available workforce/unpaid-worker numbers and a two-worker delegation do not establish crowd size.

protester_violence.summary: No explicit verified account of protester violence or its absence at the January action.

end_date.summary: No verified last public action or episode closure; end remains unknown. Additional Coding Procedure unavailable.

state_response.summary: No specific verified attribution of any of the seven coded state responses to this gathering. Earlier harms and related policy statements do not establish responses here.

notes: Provisional lead only. A February search discovery recalls a mid-January protest outside the shipyard involving MP Miro Bulj; that article was inaccessible. Opened January13 report establishes Bulj speaking with two workers, not a qualifying mass gathering. Demands seek wage payment and state intervention rather than solely a private employer dispute, but their relationship to an executed January public protest requires confirmation. January18 headquarters formation by a few workers is not a mass-action start. January29 negotiations and wage promises are not assigned as accommodation without action linkage.
open_questions: Recover contemporary account identifying actual public gathering date, attendance and state-directed demands.
Distinguish press conference, headquarters formation, industrial stoppage and public protest.
Determine organizer, independent evidence, continuity and closure.

title: Rally seeking fair treatment of police official Matko Klarić
organizer: Friends, family and colleagues of Matko Klarić
threshold_50_evidence: Opened contemporary article explicitly reports more than100 people outside police headquarters.

start_date.summary: Both Jan24 reports identify the Sunday gathering occurring that day.

location.summary: Outside Dubrovnik police headquarters; Vila Palma named by local search discovery.

organizer.summary: Friends, family and colleagues initiated the support gathering.

demands.summary: Banners call for justice and direct the minister to attend to alleged unfair disciplinary treatment.

participants.summary: Explicit more than100 people; lower bound101 follows directly, upper bound unknown.

protester_violence.summary: HINA report explicitly calls the protest peaceful.

end_date.summary: No verified last public action or episode closure; end remains unknown. Additional Coding Procedure unavailable.

state_response.summary: No specific verified attribution of any of the seven coded state responses to this gathering. Earlier harms and related policy statements do not establish responses here.

notes: Demonstrators disputed disciplinary treatment of a police official accused of sexual harassment; banners addressed the minister and demanded justice. This is a demand concerning domestic state conduct, rather than an electoral support rally. Index attendance account credits Dubrovački Dnevnik, whose original article could not be opened. Police knowledge/non-prevention and subsequent disciplinary decisions are retained as context, not coded response. This Matko Klarić is distinct from gym owner Andrija Klarić.
open_questions: Recover the local original and independent attendance confirmation.
Establish whether later gatherings occurred and episode closure.
Review demand category and additional Coding Procedure boundaries.

title: Antifascist gathering calling for legal action against Ustasha symbols
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Modest gathering is described; twenty/thirty NGOs count organizations, not people.

start_date.summary: Jan27 contemporary body places the gathering on Holocaust Remembrance Day.

location.summary: Square of Victims of Fascism in Zagreb.

organizer.summary: Antifascist League participation identified; exact organizer not verified in opened evidence.

demands.summary: Domestic legislative, prosecutorial and state-funding demands concerning Ustasha symbols and Holocaust denial.

participants.summary: Modest gathering; no attendance figure. NGO signatory counts cannot substitute.

protester_violence.summary: No explicit description establishing violence or absence of violence.

end_date.summary: No verified last public action or episode closure; end remains unknown. Additional Coding Procedure unavailable.

state_response.summary: No specific verified attribution of any of the seven coded state responses to this gathering. Earlier harms and related policy statements do not establish responses here.

notes: RFE/RL describes the public gathering at Trg žrtava fašizma alongside NGO calls for stronger sanctions, withdrawal of state funding for denialist activity and school visits to Jasenovac. HINA search discovery explicitly connects reading demands to that gathering, but its body could not be opened. Antifascist League president Zoran Pusić participated; organizer remains unconfirmed. Holocaust commemorations and officials' general statements are not assumed responses to this gathering.
open_questions: Find numerical or clear qualitative evidence supporting at least50 people.
Confirm organizer and full demand-to-gathering relationship in accessible original.
Establish closure and whether commemoration and demand action form one eligible event.

title: Hospitality owners' shopping-centre carpark meeting
threshold_50_evidence: Opened HINA report estimates about80 people attending, but eligibility as a public protest remains unresolved.

start_date.summary: Jan30 report identifies Saturday meeting on the publication day.

location.summary: Shopping-centre carpark in Zagreb; centre name unrecovered.

organizer.summary: Informal self-initiated meeting of hospitality owners.

demands.summary: Participant requests national COVID authorities reconsider the operating ban and permit work.

participants.summary: About80 owners; approximate estimate supplies threshold indication, no exact numerical bounds.

end_date.summary: No verified last public action or episode closure; end remains unknown. Additional Coding Procedure unavailable.

state_response.summary: No specific verified attribution of any of the seven coded state responses to this gathering. Earlier harms and related policy statements do not establish responses here.

notes: Saturday carpark meeting included owners from Zagreb, Karlovac and other cities, with a participant calling for the national COVID team to permit work. It may be a planning/coordination meeting rather than the required public protest. Reopening on February1 and the February3 rally were future plans in January articles; they are not shifted into January. The February3 executed rally is separately forward-linked.
open_questions: Establish public access, protest character and state-facing action of the Jan30 meeting.
Identify shopping centre and full organizer.
Resolve relationship to Feb3 without merging separate actions automatically.

title: BBB supporters' march protesting police repression

location.site: City streets, police station and water tower

organizer: BBB supporters from Vukovar and surrounding area
threshold_50_evidence: Opened contemporary PRESS032 report estimates about80 marchers. Later reproduced participant statement says roughly100; neither is exact.

start_date.summary: Jan30 contemporaneous report says today; Jan31 main text Saturday and reproduced statement yesterday support Jan30, despite conflicting image caption.

location.summary: Vukovar streets, past police station toward water tower.

organizer.summary: BBB supporters from city and surrounding area; formal organizer not established.

demands.summary: Police repression grievance reported from supporter circles; reproduced BBB statement explicitly directs protest message to station chief.

participants.summary: About80 in local report, roughly100 in advocacy statement; no exact min/max.

protester_violence.summary: Police spokesman explicitly describes peaceful march with no public-order violation.

end_date.summary: No verified last public action or episode closure; end remains unknown. Additional Coding Procedure unavailable.

state_response.summary: No specific verified attribution of any of the seven coded state responses to this gathering. Earlier harms and related policy statements do not establish responses here.

notes: Marchers passed the police station toward the water tower. Participant statement reproduced Jan31 directs a protest message at the police-station chief. Official and supporter claims about an earlier police-station confrontation conflict; those earlier arrests and alleged beatings are grievances, not responses or protester violence at this march. Later republication carries a Sunday image caption conflicting with Saturday text; Jan30 contemporary report and Jan31 statement's yesterday favor Jan30. Police monitoring is not a coded accommodation or ignore response.
open_questions: Obtain original RadioVukovar and contemporaneous participant statement, verify independence.
Resolve mixed Saturday/Sunday caption and smaller-groups versus whole-gathering detail.
Establish closure, follow-up and whether any specific coded state response occurred.
